nodes.title: English Home Language
nodes.description: English Home Language for Grade 9 covering Listening and Speaking, Reading and Viewing, Writing and Presenting, and Language Structures and Conventions across four terms.

nodes.title: Term 1
nodes.description: Term 1: Novel, drama, short story, informational texts. FAT1: Oral — prepared reading (20 pts). FAT2: Essay — argumentative/discursive (40 pts). FAT3: Response to texts (70 pts).

nodes.title: Novel and Short Story
nodes.description: Listening and Speaking: prepared oral reading (FAT1, 20 pts) — tone, voice, pace, expression, eye contact; listen and respond to a novel/drama extract; critical listening for argument and bias. Reading and Viewing: novel — in-depth character development, theme exploration, setting, narrative voice, irony; short story — plot structure: exposition, rising action, climax, falling action, resolution; literary devices: imagery, symbolism, allusion. Writing and Presenting: argumentative/discursive essay (FAT2, 40 pts, weeks 7-8) — structure: introduction, body paragraphs with topic sentences, counterargument, conclusion; logical argumentation, evidence, formal register. Language Structures and Conventions: complex sentence structures; subordination and coordination; reported speech nuances; vocabulary: connotation, denotation, register.

nodes.title: Drama and Informational Texts
nodes.description: Listening and Speaking: group discussion or debate on issues from drama; listening to a speech; identifying rhetorical devices. Reading and Viewing: drama — dramatic conventions: soliloquy, aside, dramatic irony, symbolism; newspaper feature or magazine article; reading comprehension strategies: skimming, scanning, detailed reading; fact vs opinion; writer's purpose and bias. Writing and Presenting: transactional — report or summary; informational writing conventions; web journal or blog post. Language Structures and Conventions: modal verbs; impersonal passive; sentence variety; paragraph cohesion; formal punctuation: semi-colon, colon, dash.

nodes.title: Term 2
nodes.description: Term 2: Poetry, folk tale, novel, non-fiction texts. FAT4: Transactional writing (20 pts). FAT5: Mid-year exam — Response to texts (70 pts).

nodes.title: Poetry and Folk Tale
nodes.description: Listening and Speaking: oral presentation on a poem or storytelling (folk tale performance); voice, intonation, body language; peer critique. Reading and Viewing: poetry — advanced analysis: extended metaphor, paradox, irony, allusion, tone shifts; comparing poems; folk tale — oral tradition features: moral, symbolism, cultural context, characterisation, plot. Writing and Presenting: creative response to poetry or folk tale; descriptive or narrative essay connecting to literature. Language Structures and Conventions: language of comparison and analysis; complex figurative language; etymology; formal literary vocabulary.

nodes.title: Non-Fiction and Transactional Texts
nodes.description: Listening and Speaking: panel discussion or interview; active listening and note-taking; summarise and evaluate arguments. Reading and Viewing: non-fiction texts: biography, autobiography, article; visual text: infographic or political cartoon; critical reading for bias, propaganda, stereotyping. Writing and Presenting: transactional texts (FAT4, 20 pts): formal letter, report, or précis; conventions of professional writing; summary writing. Language Structures and Conventions: tense consistency; active/passive voice advanced use; nominalization; concord rules; formal register vocabulary.

nodes.title: Term 3
nodes.description: Term 3: Creative Writing Project. FAT6: CWP Research (20 pts) + Write-up (30 pts) = 50 pts. FAT7: Oral — CWP Presentation (20 pts, begin T3 conclude T4). FAT8: Response to Literature (30 pts).

nodes.title: Creative Writing Project — Research, Writing and Oral
nodes.description: Listening and Speaking: oral preparation for CWP presentation (FAT7, 20 pts); group discussions and feedback. Reading and Viewing: research reading — variety of texts and sources; literary texts from all three prescribed genres (novel/drama, poetry, short story/folk tale); analytical reading for CWP. Writing and Presenting: CWP Phase 1 Research (FAT6, 20 pts, weeks 3-4): research notes, bibliography, graphic organiser; CWP Phase 2 Write-up (FAT6, 30 pts, weeks 5-6): final written product in chosen genre; FAT8 Response to Literature (30 pts): poetry (compulsory), novel or drama, short story or folk tale. Language Structures and Conventions: advanced stylistic choices; genre conventions mastery; argument structure in creative non-fiction; critical vocabulary.

nodes.title: Term 4
nodes.description: Term 4: Conclude oral (FAT7); transactional texts; revision; end-of-year exam (FAT9 transactional 20 pts + FAT10 Paper 2 Response to texts 70 pts).

nodes.title: Transactional Texts, Revision and Examination
nodes.description: Listening and Speaking: conclude FAT7 oral presentations; final peer assessment. Reading and Viewing: transactional texts — cover letter, CV, e-mail, minutes, memorandum; revision of all literary genres and text types; past examination papers. Writing and Presenting: cover letter and CV writing; transactional texts for FAT9 (20 pts, exam preparation); FAT10 end-of-year examination Paper 2 — Response to texts (70 pts): novel/drama, poetry, short story/folk tale. Language Structures and Conventions: comprehensive revision of all Grade 9 language structures; grammatical analysis and correction; vocabulary consolidation.
